scene_objective: Veraine finally steps into view and argues her case through questions that keep tightening around Ben and Kael.
opening_mode: Veraine steps forward and extends a hand — calm, precise, the gesture of someone who treats negotiation as professional courtesy. Ben would prefer a monster. Monsters are easier to fight.

key_beats.beat_description: Veraine steps forward and extends a hand in greeting — calm, composed, military bearing beneath academic refinement
Veraine opens with a question whose premise is the Weave's imposition; Ben answers a smaller piece of it and Veraine's next question incorporates his answer and advances
The philosophy emerges through three or four exchanges — Weave as framework, release as mercy, binary as a thousand years of war — always questions with answers she already knows, never declarations
Veraine turns to Kael and addresses him by name, her voice shifting to something specific and personal — the pitch calibrated precisely to his history rather than to generic recruitment
Kael stands motionless through the recruitment pitch, his face a mask that costs visible effort to maintain
Veraine's final question of the scene is to Kael — about what he concluded inside the wall. She does not require an answer.

turning_point.trigger: Veraine turns toward Kael and asks — in her Socratic register — why he would defend institutional frameworks that used his Force-sensitivity as building material, invoking their shared infrastructure-
turning_point.shift: Veraine turns toward Kael and asks — in her Socratic register — why he would defend institutional frameworks that used his Force-sensitivity as building material, invoking their shared infrastructure-

closing_beat: Veraine's final question before the scene ends is to Kael — soft, specific, not theatrical: a question about what he concluded during the centuries in the wall, when he had nothing to do but conclude. She does not need an answer aloud. She needs the question to sit where Kael stores answers.

emotional_arc.shift: Guarded assessment -> the unsettling experience of being asked questions whose shape presumes the conclusion -> the genuine pull of the Kael pitch -> Kael's assembling silence

anti_patterns: Do not open with a monologue from Veraine—the Socratic register is the structural answer to the risk of villain-monologue.
Do not have Ben successfully counter Veraine's argument by matching her register—every time he tries, she asks another question.
Do not resolve Kael's recruitment pitch in this scene—his silence contains an answer that will surface later.
Do not present Veraine's philosophy as obviously wrong—the book must make the distinction between correct diagnosis and catastrophic solution feelable, not assertable.
Do not have Veraine perform her argument theatrically—she is a theorist conducting an inquiry, not a villain selling a pitch.
Treat her as precise, patient, and intellectually dangerous—she does not need a speech; she needs control of the room.
